title: Daillé: honor of the saints consists in praise and imitation
source_text: XLIII. Postea vero honorem, quem & Angelis & Sanctis caelo receptis nobis deferri par est, & divinorum & Ecclesiasticorum auctorum sententia, his duobus totum contineri censet, τῇ εὐφημίᾳ καὶ τῇ μιμήσει, laude & imitatione. Quorum illud prius in eo situm est, ut bene praeclareque de iis, veluti de eximiis Dei ministris, sentiamus ac loquamur: alterum vero hoc constat, ut eorum mores, & quod communi Domino ac Deo praestiterunt obsequium, fideliter ac studiose imitemur. De objecto cultus religiosi lib. 3. cap. 1.
pass_a_gloss: But afterwards he judges that the honor which it is fitting for us to render both to Angels and to Saints received into heaven, by the judgment both of the divine and the Ecclesiastical authors, is wholly contained in these two, in eulogy and in imitation, praise and imitation. Of which the former is placed in this, that we think and speak well and nobly of them, as of excellent ministers of God: but the other consists in this, that we faithfully and zealously imitate their manners, and the obedience which they rendered to the common Lord and God. On the Object of Religious Worship, book 3, chapter 1.
pass_b_english: Daillé then holds that the honor we rightly give to the angels and to the saints received into heaven is, by the judgment of both the inspired and the church writers, entirely contained in two things: in good report and in imitation, that is, praise and imitation.

The first means thinking and speaking well and highly of them as outstanding servants of God. The second means imitating faithfully and earnestly their way of life and the obedience they gave to their Lord and God, who is ours as well. (On the Object of Religious Worship, book 3, chapter 1.)

lemmas.gloss: of the divine (biblical) and Ecclesiastical authors

choices.why: Daillé distinguishes biblical from church authors; 'inspired' makes the contrast plain in English.
